Yes—on the pasted cells, the section transitions are more distinguishable without fragmenting item interiors. I found no blocking defect in this bounded change by source inspection. That is an engineering/design judgment, not PO acceptance or an independently verified test result.

Established basis: the September 9 consultation recovered at @session:default/run_4ee2883ee9a14bca94e717104b156585 recommended stronger section boundaries while preserving compact label/detail grouping and the numbered spine. Travis’s reported difficulty was locating sections; “vertical rhythm” remained a tentative diagnosis.

The supplied after/intake-72x35-offset0.txt and after/observatory-72x35-offset0.txt support the intended improvement. The larger breaks and outer-margin rules mark the sequence and notes as sections, while the connector-only inter-item row remains visibly subordinate. Wrapped labels and their details remain adjacent. The chronology’s approximate-time qualification and unknown-cause caveats remain intact in the displayed text. I would not add label/detail gaps.

The measurement/render split looks consistent for these fixed landmarks. paragraph(block) measures a heading plus text; draw renders the heading separately and subtracts its row from text visibility and scrolling. Although the first rule is measured at the narrower item width and drawn at the outer width, the supplied fixed landmarks fit without wrapping, so I see no divergence here. That equivalence depends on retaining the one-row landmark invariant.

The bottom-orphan branch also looks coherent: it withholds a lone landmark and makes PageDown target the deferred block’s start. Fitted-block snapping permits that start. I do not see a new skip or stall introduced by that branch.

Two small findings are worth recording.

In draw, continues is set before the heading-deferral check. When only a landmark would fit, the entire block is withheld, yet the footer can say “paragraph continues” even though that paragraph never appeared. This is a minor disclosure mismatch, not observed content loss. Determine continuation after deciding whether the block will actually render, or distinguish deferred content from a displayed paragraph’s continuation.

In after/intake-80x24-offset65535.txt, End begins with the connector-only “01 │” row immediately before item 02. That is mechanically consistent with gap(Some(index)) being a legal fitted-block position, but visually it looks like an empty item fragment. It is a small navigation blemish, not evidence of detached author text, and may predate this change. I would not make a broader scrolling redesign part of this section-rhythm patch.

One qualification remains important: after/intake-80x24-offset0.txt still cuts the mandatory-prerequisite detail before “that permission exists.” The visible label retains “Only after donor permission is recorded,” and the footer explicitly marks continuation, so this is not an unmarked qualification loss. Nevertheless, “item interiors remain compact” is supported; “qualifications always remain fully visible with their labels” would be an overclaim. Paragraph-safe positioning is not semantic-unit pagination.

Limitations: I inspected the pasted source and textual cells, not live styling, the complete source, validators, tests, hashes, or terminal behavior. The reported passing example tests and Clippy remain supplied evidence; the full gate is pending. Travis still needs to judge whether the clearer boundaries earn their scrolling cost. Nothing here establishes that he has accepted the result.
note: Dottie evidence/context, not implementation authorization. No automatic retry.
